To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
radiative corrections to the neutrino parameters can be large, and that these corrections are not necessarily small in comparison to the experimental error bars on the neutrino parameters.

radiative corrections can be important for the determination of the neutrino mass scale, that radiative corrections could be the origin of the solar neutrino mass splitting if the small angle solution is realized, and that the atmospheric neutrino mass splitting is probably not determined by radiative corrections.
radiative effects can be important for the interpretation of solar and atmospheric neutrinos, and that the small angle MSWSolution is the most natural one in the Standard Model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the physical implications of radiative corrections for neutrino physics? What can be learned from the renormalization group evolution of the neutrino parameters?
the question of how much the measured neutrino data could depend on the unknown physics at the high energy scale and, in this way, provide information about the latter.
the interplay between neutrino physics and radiative effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
radiative corrections can be important for neutrino physics and must be taken into account in the analysis of the experimental data, but they cannot explain all the observed phenomena.
the present data are consistent with the simplest neutrino mixing scheme, but the radiative corrections could be important for the determination of the physical neutrino parameters.
the present experimental data are not yet precise enough to allow a definite conclusion about the origin of the observed neutrino masses and mixing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
radiative corrections are very important in understanding the origin of small neutrino masses and mixing.
the radiative effects are not important in the determination of neutrino masses and mixings but could be important in the determination some of the neutrino CP -violating parameters.
the renormalization group analysis is a powerful tool for testing the theoretical naturalness of the existing solutions to neutrino oscillation problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radiative corrections to neutrino masses are not negligible, and should be taken into account in future neutrino physics analyses.
the radiative effects are potentially large, and their study is an indispensable ingredient in any future analysis of neutrino data.
the renormalization group effects are not small and should not be neglected.
